title: The 10 Best Diagonal Cutting Pliers
subtitle: Ranked from live Amazon data — best-sellers, real ratings, honest trade-offs.
intro: We ranked 10 of Amazon's best-selling diagonal cutting pliers (side cutters, or dikes) on star rating, review volume and the features that change how they cut: a high-leverage joint, hardened edges, a comfort grip and a flush-cut blade. They run from a $9.98 CRAFTSMAN to the $41.15 KNIPEX 74 22 200, and include standard 6- to 8-inch cutters, a 9-inch ironworkers' pair and a 5-inch flush cutter. Mixed pliers sets and needle-nose pliers have their own pages.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

scoring.review_age_weighting: Listings under 24 months old with at least 30 reviews have their review count multiplied by min(2, 24 / age in months, age floored at 6) before scoring; older listings are unchanged. Listing age is Amazon's Date First Available, or an estimate from the ASIN when the listing does not show it.

buyers_guide.q: What's the difference between diagonal cutters and flush cutters?
buyers_guide.a: Diagonal cutters have beveled blades that leave a slight point on the cut end and handle copper, steel and tie wire. Flush cutters have one flat side that leaves a flat end, which is what you want on zip ties and electronics leads, but they're built for small, soft wire. The Klein D275-5 on this page is a flush cutter rated to 16 AWG.

If you often cut 12 AWG copper, screws or hard wire, yes. A high-leverage design moves the rivet closer to the blades so the same squeeze cuts harder. Klein claims 36% more cutting power for the D228-8, and Crescent claims 50% for its compound-action PS5429C. For occasional cuts, a standard 6- or 7-inch pair is lighter and fits tighter spots.

Six to seven inches suits most household electrical and DIY work. Eight-inch pairs give more leverage for heavier wire, and the 9-inch Klein D248-9ST is meant for rebar tie wire. Five-inch flush cutters are for zip ties and electronics.

buyers_guide.q: What does HRC mean on the cutting edge?
buyers_guide.a: It's the Rockwell C hardness of the blade. Higher numbers hold an edge longer and cut harder wire. The KNIPEX 74 22 200 lists about 64 HRC, the KNIPEX 70 01 160 about 62 HRC, and WORKPRO lists up to 65 HRC for its high-frequency-hardened edge. Several brands here say only "induction hardened" without a number.

buyers_guide.q: Can I cut live wires with these?
buyers_guide.a: No. None of the pliers on this page are listed as 1000V insulated, so shut off the circuit first. Insulated diagonal cutters carry a 1000V rating on the handles and are sold separately.
